name: workers
description: Two side panes. Git: each folder directly inside the session's folder with the git branch checked out in it, or "no git"; /git opens it. Workers: the project's chats, who is working on what, which step, how long, and whose turn it is; /workers opens it. The app's own notes in a prompt (system reminders, side-session events, messages from another chat) are never filed as the person's instructions. A chat in the list also takes what the person answered for it on the worker board and types it in as their own words, and tells the board why one could not be typed. An answer that ends with a "For you" block the chat filed no ask for has its items filed on the board when the turn ends. After the turn in which a worker reported its step it is compacted when large (list.json "compactAbove", 250000 tokens unless set, 0 for never) or, with list.json "afterStep": "clear", cleared with /clear even when more work follows: the worker board first keeps the conversation as a log, the card moves to the new session, and the fresh conversation is told who it is, where its rules and log are, its open instructions, and to run work next. The main chat and the partners are never cleared; they are compacted at rest above the threshold. Each call of the work tool carries a request id, so a call whose answer is slow or cut off is asked again and recorded once; a board that does not answer is named with its reason, and a take it does not answer within 15 s is given up and asked again. When the person pauses all chats on the board, each chat is told at its next batch of tool calls to write its checkpoint and end its turn; after the resume the main chat is told whom to wake, and each chat holding a step its checkpoint. A chat renamed in the app follows the name the board shows it under: refused under its old name, it joins under the new one and asks once more. The chat the list names "supervisor" reads the board's health summary (work health) and files incidents (work incident), and is cleared after every turn of its own, without a log, so each sweep starts empty. Every call to the board says the mod's version, so the board sees a chat on an older mod, and each chat writes it on its card: the Workers pane shows each chat's version and, for one older than the newest, that the board has it restarted after its step. Until 0.31.0 a worker whose last report is newer than its last clear was cleared when the board named it at a take (the log refused while background work ran, a restart or a pause between); the take names no clear any more (see 0.31.0 below). Each chat tells the board its turn state, busy, idle (with background work still running or not) or asking the person, the moment it changes and with every take, so the board shows what the chat says instead of guessing; while a clear is on its way the report still goes every 5 s. The board hands out every task itself (its redesign's Part 2): the work tool has no queue, requeue or unqueue. A chat learns its name from the board by its session id (the app's title is not needed): at its start and before a prompt, at most once a minute, it asks the board who its session is and joins under that name; a card the board names under another session (a worker cleared in a new process) is moved to the chat's own session, a worker with the words of a clear. Every 20 s a chat in the list claims the board's hand jobs and does them by code, with no model turn: where the app allows its code the send-message tool with no question (an allow rule; a chat in Auto mode has its sends put to the classifier, which denies them, so without the rule it says so and gets none), it starts, wakes and resumes chats with it and, where the app allows its code both set tools with no question (an allow rule), sets a chat's model and effort with them, restarts an idle worker for a new mod (closes and reopens it) and starts a new worker by running the stored start-worker task and looks the plan's limits up when the board's newest reading is old, and takes a worker the person removed off the list and closes its chat, and archives the older chats of a worker that a newer run of its routine replaced; a worker whose task the person stops or that is removed is told at its next tool call; it says what it did. A call the app has not answered within 2 minutes gives its word back to the board in doubt (it may have gone: no other chat sends it while a late answer may come, and a late send still counts), and a chat whose call hangs or whose process has no session to call tools in claims no job until it can (0.27.1). A popup that may wait for the person shows on the board: a call that does not run long by itself (not a shell, subagent or wait) still running after a minute is filed on the board as an ask in the chat's name, in a few plain words (answered in its chat), and the chat reports itself asking, until the call goes on or its turn ends. The partner chat judges the open items of Needs your attention when the person asks for it on the board (work obsolete: it reads them with their evidence and answers one line per item; nothing is closed by it). A worker on the board's hand-over sequence (the board's setting "handover": "sequence", 0.27.0) decides no clear of its own at a turn's end: the board answers the turn's end (or a take) with one envelope, which the mod carries out once per id, in order, stopping at the first that fails: a restart (the log kept, the card marked, nothing else), a clear (the log kept, the card marked, /clear, with every guard of the clear after a step), the model and effort the board's hands already set, and the line typed into the fresh conversation together with the words a cleared chat gets, as one prompt; then it tells the board once how it went. It tells the board every answered turn's end, and while idle reads its background work anew at each 5-second ping. Without the board's hand-over it behaves as before. The mod uses no classic hooks (the app's guard skips them on a work login), so both logins behave the same. 0.28.0: the Workers pane and the chat tool's list show the board's own status for each chat, the one its page's pill says (the board's answer to a take now carries it), in bold when it needs attention; the pane reads the chats' card files itself again, and marks the line "(board not reached)", only when no status came for 120 s (a fresh chat, an older board and a chat outside the list are not marked). The Product owner's chat (list.json "owner") is compacted at rest and never cleared or taken for a worker, also when the board's answer names no role. Rollout: workers on the hand-over sequence restart onto 0.28.0 through its RESTARTING envelope; the main chat, the Advisor, its helper, the Supervisor and the Product owner through the main chat's rollout words. 0.29.0: the work tool's asset action (kind visual, music or sound effect, text, pictures, of, follows; a library pick with id and picked): every chat asks the board for an asset, and the board has the provider the person chose make it and tells the chat when it is ready; nobody runs Codex, Suno or ElevenLabs itself. 0.29.1: a /clear of the mod runs the clear on its way whatever the order of the mod's queue of /clear commands (it fell out of step with the engine's, and every later clear of that chat was refused until its restart), while that clear's session is this one, no turn runs and nothing came in since; one that may not run is dropped at once with its why. 0.30.0: every report and take tells the board the word the chat's turn runs on (the outbox id of the board's word, null for a line the person typed) and when that turn began, unchanged by a question that opens and closes within it, so the board's wait line knows instead of guessing; the envelope's outcome carries typedAt and enteredAt, the exact moments its line was typed and entered the chat; a kept board is started only after two missed pings in a row, so a landing's restart no longer starts a second board; the Workers pane line names the step the board knows the chat holds, with its time, in place of the card's task words; the take's off list is no longer read, the board's statuses say Not running; a background command or Monitor the chat started (also one the app moved to the background) keeps its report background until the app's note that it ended, or a /clear. A Monitor also leaves that count at its deadline. The clear on its way is kept in the mod's store, so a reload or a new process still runs it and settles its envelope. A board the mod starts runs detached, its output appended to its data/board.log, and outlives the chat that started it. 0.31.0: the lazy clear: no clear is ever sent alone, a worker owes its clear and gets it with its next task's envelope (a free worker stays as it is, and the mod's own clear at a turn's end when the board did not answer is gone); a clear that does not run (refused, not run within 20 s, dropped) never holds the worker: the task's line is typed anyway into the old conversation and the clear stays owed, except under the person's pause, and a /clear that comes late never clears mid-task; every stage of a clear (log saved, clear queued, cleared, refused) is told to the board the moment it happens, and the envelope's outcome says why the clear did not run (clearWhy). Words the app merged into one prompt while the chat was busy are confirmed: the turn's start tells the board each word its prompt holds typed, once, and names the turn by the first of them. The board lands first: one older than 0.31.0 reads a clear that did not run as a failed hand-over. 0.31.1 (F4, chats losing the mod): every hook answers within 5 s whatever hangs (a deadline on the mod's own waits; the board's calls are free of the budget), a subagent's turn starts and ends nothing of the list's, the work tool sleeps no more (a cut call is asked again in the background), and the card scan skips cards not written for a week and reads a card again only when its size or time changed.
